answer: A no-code app builder gives you screens and rules over your data; an agentic app adds a crew of AI agents that work the records.
Pick a builder for screens people fill in, an agentic app for follow-up work.

sections.h2: Where a no-code builder is the better pick

ul: **The sheet must stay the source.** Glide and Softr connect to Google Sheets and keep working from it. 50agents imports a copy and does not stay linked.
**Many audiences, fine-grained access.** Softr's user groups set which pages, data and actions each person reaches, and it can preview the app as one user.
**Your data is already in Airtable.** Interfaces add list, kanban, calendar, timeline and dashboard layouts to the base, with no import.
**Field teams on phones.** Glide builds apps meant for the desktop and the phone in the field.
**You want to design every step.** Builders let you shape each screen and workflow by hand, and Softr adds AI agents you configure yourself.

method.h2: How to choose between an agentic app and a builder

steps.title: Write down who does the work
steps.body: List the jobs around the data: entering it, checking it, chasing people. Mostly entering and viewing points to a builder. Mostly chasing points to an agentic app.

steps.title: Check where the data must live
steps.body: If people must keep editing the original sheet or base, choose a builder with a live link. An agentic app in 50agents imports a copy and becomes the place you edit.

steps.title: List who may see what
steps.body: Write down each group of users and what they may see and change: clients, staff, managers. Compare that list with each tool's access settings before you build anything.

steps.title: Count the follow-ups that slip
steps.body: How many leads, requests or invoices sat for a week with no next step last month? Each one is a draft an AI agent could have written for your yes.

steps.title: Build the same small job twice
steps.body: Take one list, such as open invoices, and build it in a builder and as an agentic app. Use both for a week with real, messy records.

note.text: A workflow set to email on a record change sends every time, right or wrong. Add an approval step before it reaches a client.

steps.title: Keep one place to edit
steps.body: Whichever wins, archive the other copy the day you switch. Two tools holding the same records drift apart.

captain.line: Captain builds the agentic side: an invoices desk with Collector, an AI agent that drafts a reminder a day after each due date and waits for your yes.

wrong.title: Choosing on the demo
wrong.body: A demo shows clean data and the happy path. Test with your own records, blanks, duplicates and odd date formats included.

wrong.title: The sheet and the app drift
wrong.body: People keep editing the old sheet after you import it into an agentic app. Lock or archive the sheet the day the app goes live.

wrong.title: Nobody reads what the AI agents do
wrong.body: Drafts pile up in Needs you, or get approved unread. Set ten minutes a day to clear them for the first two weeks.

faqs.q: Are Glide and Softr agentic app builders?
faqs.a: Both have added AI. Glide's own AI builds apps from your spreadsheets, and Softr has AI agents that chat with users inside an app or run on a schedule. Their center is still the screens and the workflows you design.

faqs.q: Can an agentic app stay linked to my Google Sheet?
faqs.a: Not in 50agents: it imports the sheet as a CSV or Excel file and keeps its own records. If the sheet must stay the source, Glide or Softr fit better; see [50agents vs Glide](/compare/50agents-vs-glide).

Yes. Glide Workflows start on a schedule, a webhook, an email or an action in the app. Softr Workflows start on record changes, forms and schedules, and Airtable automations on records, forms and set times.

faqs.q: Can I build a client portal either way?
faqs.a: Softr is built for client portals, with user groups that limit pages and records. A 50agents app can also serve people outside your team, on your own domain.
An agentic app in 50agents starts from one sentence and a plan you check before Build it. A no-code builder asks for more decisions up front, which is also what lets you shape every screen.

faqs.q: Can I move from a no-code builder to an agentic app later?
faqs.a: Yes, if the builder exports your table as CSV. Drop the file into a 50agents app and Captain matches the columns. A file import keeps one record per email address.
